sources: Two Middle Eastern government officials, via AP (Nov 7-8); The Guardian (Nov 7); Iran FM spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei, weekly press conference, via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Is the bridge deal a real off-ramp -- blockade relief for inspections and a reopened strait in 48 hours -- or a trap that trades permanent leverage (the blockade, $8bn) for reversible gestures?

sections.what_happened: Qatar, chief mediator, has presented a two-day 'bridge deal': DAY 1 -- the US lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports and releases part of Iran's ~$8 billion in frozen assets; Iran grants IAEA inspectors immediate access to nuclear sites bombed by US/Israeli forces. DAY 2 -- Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz under a modified Iran-Oman arrangement (not yet US-approved), temporary until a permanent Gulf deal. After that, full talks on Iran's 60%-enriched uranium stockpile (IAEA: 440.9 kg at 60%, June 13 2025). Iran is reviewing it but insists on preconditions before nuclear talks: end of blockade, sanctions relief, unfrozen assets, compensation for war damage, end of hostilities across the region including Israeli operations in Lebanon. In-window hook: Baghaei said at his Nov 9 press conference that Iran's two-day proposal to fully open Hormuz is 'the most reasonable proposal on the table'. The deal is on the table today as Trump meets Qatar PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House (~12:00 ET / 20:00 ), with VP Vance meeting him separately first.
sections.what_verified: Terms rest on AP's two anonymous regional officials, carried by multiple outlets = 1 family (AP, T1). The Guardian (T3) independently reported the same terms Nov 7. Al Jazeera (T2) carries Baghaei's in-window endorsement of the two-day proposal. Qatari PM told Al Jazeera Nov 7 negotiations had made 'substantial progress'; Qatari FM spokesman Majed al-Ansari rejected reports talks had collapsed.
sections.what_disputed: Sec. Rubio (Sunday): negotiations have made little progress, no imminent breakthrough -- directly contradicts the Qatari PM's 'substantial progress'. The proposal 'has not yet received US approval' (ToI/AP). Iran SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei (Nov 5, in Russia): Tehran refuses to reopen Hormuz or negotiate until Washington meets its seven demands. Trump on 60 Minutes: renewed strikes 'highly unlikely' IF talks progress -- conditional, not a commitment. The 440.9 kg / 60% figure is IAEA's June 13 2025 estimate, not a current measurement.
sections.why_matters: 48 hours, $8 billion, one strait: Qatar's bridge deal would lift the blockade and free frozen cash on day one -- and Iran just called it 'the most reasonable proposal on the table'. Trump meets the Qatari PM tonight.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP + IN-WINDOW HOOK -- Qatar's two-day 'bridge deal': lift the blockade + release frozen assets for IAEA access, Hormuz reopens day 2; Iran's FM spokesman calls it 'the most reasonable proposal on the table'

Trump meets the Qatari PM tonight. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the bridge deal a real off-ramp -- blockade relief for inspections and a reopened strait in 48 hours -- or a trap that trades permanent leverage (the blockade, $8bn) for reversible gestures?
